disasterNumber.def: Sequentially assigned number used to designate an event or incident declared as a disaster.  For more information on the disaster process, please visit https://www.fema.gov/disasters/how-declared

incidentType.def: The primary or official type of incident such as fire or flood. Secondary incident types may have been designated. See the designatedIncidentTypes field. For more information on incident types, please visit https://www.fema.gov/disasters/how-declared.

totalApprovedIhpAmount.def: Total amount approved in dollars under FEMAs IHP program

validRegistrations.def: Count of FEMA registration owners within the state, county, zip where the registration is valid.  In order to be a valid registration, the applicant must be in an Individual Assistance declared state and county and have registered within the FEMA designated registration period

highRiskPropertyType.def: Indicate High Risk Property Type: RL - IA Repetitve Loss; SRL - IA Severe Repetitive Loss. RL is properties impacted by 2-3 disaster declarations. SRL denotes properties impacted by 4 or more disaster declarations.

buildingDamageAmount.def: The actual cash value amount of damage to a main property in whole dollars.

countyCode.def: FIPS code uniquely identifying the primary County (e.g., 011 represents Broward County) associated with the project. Note, the County Code field may not reflect the individual county the property is located as projects can be associated with more than one county

floodEvent.def: Name given to a flooding catastrophe

id.def: Unique ID assigned to the record

netBuildingPaymentAmount.def: Net building payment amount made to insured in dollars. It is the amountPaidOnBuildingClaim minus any recovery amounts.

netContentsPaymentAmount.def: Net contents payment amount made to insured in dollars. This is the amountPaidOnContentsClaim minus recovery amounts.

netIccPaymentAmount.def: Net Increased Cost of Compliance (ICC) payment amount made to insured in dollars.

totalBuildingInsuranceCoverage.def: Total Insurance Amount in whole dollars on the Building

yearOfLoss.def: Year in which the flood loss occurred

classRating.def: The Class rating are based on aggregated points communities received for implementing floodplain activities that are higher than the minimum requirements of the National Flood Insurance Program (NFIP)

communityName.def: This is the name of the community, and is associated with the unique CID identifier. Generally, an NFIP community represents the lowest level of government with land use authority. Thus, not every city or town is recognized as its own community with the NFIP. Each state or territory determines land use authority granted to counties/parishes/boroughs, towns/cities, tribal area, etc. within their own jurisdiction

nonSfhaDiscount.def: The percentage of non Special Flood Hazard Area insurance (non-SFHA)  discount available based on the information received from the Community Rating System (CRS)

sfhaDiscount.def: The percentage of Special Flood Hazard Area (SFHA) insurance discount available based on the information received from the Community Rating System (CRS)

buildingReplacementCost.def:
Estimated cost in whole dollars to replace the building as reported by the insurer. 
NOTE: Replacement cost is not market value, and it does not include the cost of the land or contents. It is strictly the estimated cost to reconstruct the building

censusGeoid.def: Numeric code that uniquely identifies all administrative/legal and statistical geographic areas for which the Census Bureau tabulates data. In this instance, the Census GeoID is presented at the Census Block Group level. This is an address-based 12-character code that is the concatenation of fields consisting of the 2-character state FIPS code, the 3-character county FIPS code, the 6-character census tract code, and the 1-character block group code. Block numbers beginning with a zero are associated with water-only areas. Please see: https://www.census.gov/programs-surveys/geography/guidance/geo-identifiers.html

fullRiskPremium.def: The chargeable premium for a property based on its determined flood risk and the full cost to pay anticipated losses and expenses for that property.

id.def: Unique ID assigned to the record

occupancyType.def: Code indicating the use and occupancy type of the insured structure. Note, 2-digit codes are for Risk Rating 2.0 policies.  1 = Single family residence; 2 = 2 to 4 Unit residential building; 3 = Residential building with more than 4 units; 4 = Non-residential building; 6 = Non-Residential Business; 11 = Single-family residential building with the exception of a mobile home or a single residential unit within a multi unit building; 12 = A residential non-condo building with 2, 3, or 4  units seeking insurance on all units; 13 = A residential non-condo building with 5 or more units seeking insurance on all units; 14 = Residential mobile/manufactured home; 15 = Residential condo association seeking coverage on a building with one or more units; 16 = Single residential unit within a multi-unit building; 17 = Non-residential mobile/manufactured home; 18 = A non-residential building; 19 = A non-residential unit within a multi-unit building;

policyCost.def: Calculated in dollars by adding together calculated premium, reserve fund assessment, federal policy fee, and HFIAA surcharge

policyCount.def: Insured units in an active status. A policy contract ceases to be in an active status as of the cancellation date or the expiration date. Residential Condominium Building Association Policy (RCBAP) contracts are stored as a single policy contract but insure multiple units and therefore represent multiple policies

policyEffectiveDate.def: The effective date of the flood policy. When time is not specified in the field, it will default to T00:00:00.000Z. Effective March 1, 1995, the standard waiting period for new business applications and for endorsements increasing coverage is 30 days from the date of application and the presentment of premium.  (Example:  A policy applied for on April 3 would become effective at 12:01 a.m. on May 3.)

policyTerminationDate.def: Date upon which the cancellation of a flood insurance policy becomes effective - either because it was cancelled or lapsed. When time is not specified in the field, it will default to T00:00:00.000Z

reportedZipCode.def: 5-digit Postal  Zip Code for the insured property reported by WYO partners

totalBuildingInsuranceCoverage.def: Total Insurance Amount in whole dollars on the Building

totalContentsInsuranceCoverage.def: Total Insurance Amount in whole dollars on the Contents

totalInsurancePremiumOfThePolicy.def: Total Insurance Premium of the Policy in whole dollars. Negative values indicate a refund.

resContractsInForce.def: National Flood Insurance Program (NFIP) Insured Residential Policy Contracts in Force (CIF) in the county. Data Source: PIVOT (system of record).

resPenetrationRate.def: NFIP insured residential structures in the county divided by all residential structures in the county. Policy Contracts in Force (CIF) is a good approximation of individual insured structures, as opposed to Policies in Force (PIF), which includes individual units within condominium structures.

resPenetrationRateSfha.def: NFIP insured residential structures in the Special Flood Hazard Area (SFHA) of the county divided by all residential structures in the SFHA of the county.
